scenario: LLEX.11.1 spells the base prefixes `0x`, `0b` and `0o`, lowercase only. `0XFF` is therefore not a hex literal: by LLEX.11.3.1 a digit directly followed by a letter is a unit literal, so it is `0` of the unit `XFF`, which nothing declares. A compiler that takes an uppercase prefix as well reads `0XFF` as 255 and compiles this. The runtimes' `String::Int?` parse refuses `"0X1F"` (logical/LCST.4.5.7_int_non_literals_are_null).
rules_ds:
schema Flags scope logical:
    mask: Int key

rule r:
    Flags f where f.mask == 0XFF
->
    log info "never"
